items.title: Technology skills are among the fastest-growing in demand worldwide
items.summary: The World Economic Forum's 2025 survey of employers reports that AI and big data, networks and cybersecurity, and technological literacy are among the fastest-growing skills, alongside analytical thinking, resilience and flexibility.
items.sourceName: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025

items.title: Large job creation and displacement are expected at the same time
items.summary: Employers surveyed by the World Economic Forum expect both substantial job creation and displacement by 2030, with a net positive effect. They also expect a large share of workers' skills to need updating, which makes reskilling a central workforce priority.
items.sourceName: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025

items.title: Skills required for the same job are changing quickly
items.summary: LinkedIn's Economic Graph research on AI at work suggests the skills needed in many jobs are shifting, which increases the value of adaptable, transferable skills alongside technical ones.
items.sourceName: LinkedIn Economic Graph, Future of Work Report: AI at Work

items.title: Generative AI use at work is already widespread
items.summary: Microsoft and LinkedIn's 2024 Work Trend Index found that a large majority of knowledge workers surveyed already use generative AI at work, and that many employers say they would hire a less experienced candidate who has AI skills.
items.sourceName: Microsoft and LinkedIn, 2024 Work Trend Index

items.title: Generative AI could change a large share of knowledge-work tasks
items.summary: McKinsey estimates generative AI could add large economic value across functions such as customer operations, marketing and sales, software engineering and R&D, mainly by changing how tasks within jobs are done.
items.sourceName: McKinsey, The economic potential of generative AI

items.title: Most exposure to generative AI is augmentation, not full automation
items.summary: An ILO global analysis finds that most occupations are more likely to be partly augmented than fully automated by generative AI, with clerical work the most exposed, and stresses the importance of job quality and policy.
items.sourceName: International Labour Organization, Generative AI and Jobs

items.title: A large share of jobs worldwide is exposed to AI
items.summary: An IMF staff note estimates that around 40 percent of global employment is exposed to AI, with higher exposure in advanced economies and mixed effects on inequality, which makes skills and policy choices important.
items.sourceName: International Monetary Fund, Gen-AI: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Work

items.title: Developers are adopting AI tools quickly, with mixed trust
items.summary: The Stack Overflow 2024 Developer Survey reports that a large majority of respondents are using or planning to use AI tools in development, while many remain cautious about accuracy.

items.title: Cybersecurity teams report persistent staffing and skills gaps
items.summary: ISC2's 2024 workforce study estimates a continuing global shortfall of cybersecurity professionals and highlights AI and cloud security among the skills teams most want to develop.

items.title: AI is changing how people interact with software
items.summary: Nielsen Norman Group argues that AI introduces a new interaction paradigm in which users state intent in natural language, raising the importance of user research and interaction design judgement.
items.sourceName: Nielsen Norman Group, AI Is First New UI Paradigm in 60 Years

items.title: Education systems are defining AI competencies for students and teachers
items.summary: UNESCO has published AI competency frameworks for students and for teachers, covering human-centred mindset, ethics, AI techniques and system design, to guide responsible use of AI in education.
items.sourceName: UNESCO, AI competency frameworks for students and teachers

items.title: Malaysia's national digital policy emphasises digital talent
items.summary: The MyDIGITAL initiative sets Malaysia's national direction for digital economy growth and includes a focus on developing digital talent and adoption across sectors, which is relevant context for local graduates.
